q: A die is thrown once. What is the probability of getting an even number?
exp: Even outcomes are 2, 4 and 6. Therefore, probability = 3/6 = 1/2.

q: A die is thrown once. What is the probability of getting a number greater than 4?
exp: Numbers greater than 4 are 5 and 6. Probability = 2/6 = 1/3.

q: A die is thrown once. What is the probability of getting a prime number?
exp: Prime numbers on a die are 2, 3 and 5. Probability = 3/6 = 1/2.

q: Two dice are thrown together. What is the probability that the sum is 7?
exp: The six favorable outcomes are (1,6), (2,5), (3,4), (4,3), (5,2) and (6,1). Probability = 6/36 = 1/6.

q: Two dice are thrown together. What is the probability of getting the same number on both dice?
exp: Doubles are (1,1) through (6,6), giving 6 favorable outcomes out of 36. Probability = 1/6.

q: A coin is tossed three times. What is the probability of getting exactly two heads?
exp: There are 3 ways to get exactly two heads: HHT, HTH and THH. Probability = 3/8.

q: Two coins are tossed together. What is the probability of getting at least one head?
exp: Outcomes are HH, HT, TH and TT. Three contain at least one head, so probability = 3/4.

q: A coin is tossed three times. What is the probability of getting three heads?
exp: There is only one favorable outcome, HHH, out of 8 equally likely outcomes. Probability = 1/8.

q: A card is drawn from a standard deck of 52 cards. What is the probability of getting an ace?
exp: There are 4 aces in a deck of 52 cards. Probability = 4/52 = 1/13.

q: A card is drawn from a standard deck. What is the probability of getting a king?
exp: There are 4 kings among 52 cards. Probability = 4/52 = 1/13.

q: A card is drawn from a standard deck of 52 cards. What is the probability of getting a heart?
exp: There are 13 hearts in a 52-card deck. Probability = 13/52 = 1/4.

q: A card is drawn from a standard deck. What is the probability of getting a face card?
exp: There are 12 face cards: 4 kings, 4 queens and 4 jacks. Probability = 12/52 = 3/13.

q: A bag contains 5 red balls and 3 blue balls. One ball is drawn at random. What is the probability of getting a blue ball?
exp: There are 3 blue balls out of 8 total balls. Probability = 3/8.

q: A bag contains 4 red and 6 blue balls. Two balls are drawn without replacement. What is the probability that both are red?
A bag contains 4 red and 6 blue balls. Two balls are drawn without replacement. What is the probability of getting at least one red ball?
exp: Use the complement. Probability of no red = both blue = 6/10 × 5/9 = 1/3. Therefore, probability of at least one red = 1−1/3 = 2/3.
